name: 'If Stone Could Speak’: Day of Craft
description:
Experience hands-on techniques with experts and artists in two nearby locations. Experiment with stone, paper sculpting and weaving. 
Part of a cultural programme delivered by City of London Corporation and Cheapside Business Alliance, produced by URBAN LEARNERS, encouraging discussion on reuse and heritage focused on historic granite stones repurposed as inclusive seating by St Paul’s Cathedral.

name: All Saints Church, Tooting
description: A Gothic revival church of cathedral proportions completed in 1906 by Temple Moore with Italian baroque features from Bologna and Florence. Excellent acoustic design has enabled recordings from London Chamber Choir, Paul McCartney's tribute to Linda, Pavarotti, Placido Domingo, and many more!
address: All Saints Church, Tooting, Brudenell Road, SW17 8DQ

name: Bankside Yards Historic Arches:  then, now, next
description: An architectural talk exploring the story of the historic Bankside Yards railway arches and their transformation into a new cultural destination on London’s Bankside. Now reopening after 150 years hidden from the public, the talk will offer an opportunity to discover how historic infrastructure can be reimagined to create vibrant new spaces while preserving the character and stories of the past.

name: Beckenham Library
description: Beckenham Library is a busy public library,  which first opened in March 1939. It has been extended over the years and was extensively refurbished and re-opened in 2025. The library includes the study area with original wooden features, children's library with arts-themed  mural by artist Alice Patullo, and community space. The Battle of Britain Lace Panel has recently been installed.
address: Beckenham Library, Beckenham Road, Beckenham, BR3 4PE

name: Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan
description: The Bhavan UK is part of the global Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan movement, with 110 centres worldwide, including 105 in India. As a leading centre for Indian arts, culture and education in London, The Bhavan promotes shared cultural understanding and brings people together through music, dance, language, philosophy and community learning.

name: Burlington House: Linnean Society of London
description: The world's oldest active biological society. Founded in 1788, the Society takes its name from the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus whose botanical, zoological and library collections have been in its keeping since 1829.

name: Charing Cross Library
description: The building has had many incarnations since its construction in the 1890s as a woolen warehouse.   It became a home to the Italian Benevolent Society, then a fascist club, a serviceman's club, and now a library with the largest publicly accessible collection of Chinese language books in the UK.

name: Chiswick Town Hall
description: Built initially as a vestry, it was later extended. Victorian and Edwardian interiors with rich tiles and stunning stained glass, one of the most beautiful Victorian interiors in London.

name: Corbett Community Library
description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
address: Corbett Community Library, 103 Torridon Road, SE6 1RQ

name: Crossing the Boundary, breaking the ground
description: The walk crosses the Boundary Road which divides Westminster and Camden and focuses on projects that represent ground-breaking trends in architecture of 1960-70s while also reflecting on the era's passing and its long-lasting influences.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Designer-led tour of Gordon Street, Bloomsbury
description: Working with University College London and Camden Council, LDA Design, Norman Rourke Pryme and Darryl Moore have transformed Gordon Street, on the north side of Gordon Square in Bloomsbury to create a new 'college campus' for students, staff and the wider community. This has repurposed a road to create valuable new city green space. Find out what they did and how.
address: 22 Gordon Street, The Bartlett School of Architecture, WC1H 0QB

name: Dominion Theatre
description: A Grade II listed art deco theatre in the heart of London. Built in 1929, this stylish building has had a varied and colourful history as a cinema, variety hall and music venue, as well as its original and current life as a theatre.

name: Exploring Spring Grove Isleworth
description: Centred on Spring Grove House, once Sir Joseph Banks home, the 1850s vision was for a neighbourhood with grand villas designed by John Taylor Jr.. Today's  wider architecture includes a former college by John Norton & P Massey, plus quirky arts & crafts properties.
address: Forecourt, Isleworth Railway Station, London Road, Isleworth, TW7 4BX

name: Fear and loathing on the South Bank of the Thames
description: For centuries the South Bank of the Thames sat outside the historic City of London's jurisdiction — and beyond its moral gaze. This walk traces how that freedom shaped the unique buildings and streets of Southwark, and how the regenerated riverfront we see today has preserved, adapted or quietly erased that past.
address: Bridge Theatre, 3 Potters Flds Pk, SE1 2SG

name: Film Locations of the City
description: A walk around places in the City you might recognise (or not) from the silver screen. Visit the impressive sites used in major films, including Harry Potter, Mission Impossible, James Bond, and many more.
address: Leadenhall Market (under central atrium by Lamb Tavern), EC3V 1LT

name: Fitzrovia Chapel
description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road
description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
address: Paradise works, 142 Lea Bridge Road, E5 9RB

name: Freud Museum London
description: Freud Museum London is the final home of the founder of psychoanalysis, Sigmund Freud, where he and his family moved to flee Nazi persecution in 1938. Freud's famous study has been preserved as he left it upon his death in 1939, while the rest of the home has been carefully transformed into a Museum celebrating the life and work of Sigmund and his daughter Anna, a pioneering child psychologist.

name: From Limehouse to Canary Wharf
description: Medieval industry, imperial trade, immigration, poverty, wartime destruction and modern regeneration have all left their mark on the Limehouse area. This walking tour covers a range of architects and architecture from C18th to C21st.

name: Hidden City: Lost rivers, super sewers and sacred springs
description: Join this enjoyable stroll through the City of London, exploring the story of water and how it continues to shape the place we know today. We will follow in the footsteps of ancient Romans and famous Londoners such as Dick Whittington and Samuel Pepys, and discover how a forgotten river, ingenious water wheels and vast sewers have transformed life in the City from earliest days to the present.

name: IMPACT Community Arts Centre
description: We are a theatre company for performers and artists with learning disabilities in the West London area. We will put on an exhibition of artworks and costumes at our Community Arts Centre.
address: Ealing Central Sports Ground, Horsenden Lane South, Greenford

name: Ironmongers' Hall
description: The Hall stands on land which was bought in 1922: construction work, which was undertaken by Holland, Hannen & Cubitts, started that year and the Hall was opened on 17 June 1925. Decorated in the Arts & Crafts style, and resplendent with art and treasures, visitors will gain access to areas not normally open to the public and will be guided by real Company members.

name: Islington New River walking tour
description: This walking tour will follow the course one of the earliest public infrastructure projects in London, the 400 year old New River aqueduct. Explore a history of innovative public housing developments in one of the most densely populated parts of London and end at New River Head, a striking example of public utility architecture now being repurposed for arts and culture.
address: Outside Canonbury Overground Station, Wallace Road, N1 2PG

name: JW3 London
description: JW3 is the first and only Jewish Community Centre and arts venue of its kind to exist in UK. Architecturally award-winning, we are an open and welcoming Jewish space that brings different people together, strengthens identities, and builds community through arts, culture, education, and social action.

name: Jewish Westminster
description: This walk will look at the history of Jewish Communities in England, starting with the medieval period through to the expulsion in 1290 and readmission under Oliver Cromwell in 1656. It will also look at some of the Jewish people living as Christians between these times and the key contributions Jews have made to many of the key landmarks in London  as well as England's political life.
address: Charing Cross Station - Eleanor Cross, WC2N 5HS

name: London National Park City Visitors Centre
description: London is the world's first National Park City, and our visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street is the entry point to hundreds of places to visit and things to do across a greener, healthier and wilder London.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: Money, Money, Money
description: Buried treasures, banks and bullion…. Explore the legendary wealth of the City of London and its modern-day reputation as a global centre of finance. They used to say its streets were paved with gold... This guided walk explores the historic sources of the City's money, including livery companies, global trade and the development of the banking industry, and some of the ways that manifests today.
address: City Information Centre, St Paul's Churchyard, EC4M 8BX

name: Mornington Crescent: a walk through South Camden
description: On a walk that begins and ends at Mornington Crescent station, discover how housing, industry, education, entertainment and social reform have shaped the surrounding area. Along the way, explore how buildings and public spaces have been demolished, adapted and given new lives, revealing layers of Camden's changing social history.

name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.

name: Open (Public) House! Historic Pub Tour in Croydon
description: Drink in the hidden histories of Croydon’s historic pubs with Pub Historian Charo Havermans. This Open House, we’re letting you into the secrets and fascinating stories of some of Croydon’s most iconic and historic Public Houses. Join Pub Historian and tour guide Charo Havermans as she takes you to four historic pubs in the heart of Croydon.

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that work still remaining to this day.							
During the Festival there will be opportunities to self-guide or to join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: Refugees, Radicals and Revellers in Soho
description: Hear about the history of Soho on a walk around some of the sites associated with colourful characters of yesteryear. From Soho's beginnings as a fashionable suburb in the seventeenth century up to the 1950s, I regale you with delicious snippets of history. We end the tour with the option of refreshments at the birthplace of British RocknRoll.
address: Tottenham Court Rd station exit 4, W1D 2DH

name: Resonance FM Studios
description: Resonance FM is a pioneering, non-profit community radio station, with a studio at 7 Risborough Street, Southwark, London. Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.

name: Sacred Grounds / St Anne's Church and Garden
description: Start your exploration of the Open House Soho Neighbourhood with a shot of coffee, a refreshing cold drink and a bite to eat.  Explore our timeline of Soho, and our existing display on the church's history.   Relax in our calm and welcoming gardens.

name: Sanderson Hotel: A Modernist Landmark Reimagined
description: The landmarked 1950s building has been transformed by Philippe Starck into a surreal Cocteau like dream world, epitomising a new luxury that is smart, pared down and tempered with a healthy dose of wit and irony. With rooms designed by designer Tim Andreas of Banjo, the rooms maintain their sense of whimsy while offering state of the art details and luxurious touches at every turn.

name: Sex in the City - a tour of Covent Garden's history
description: This is a walking tour that delves into the scandalous history of Covent Garden. This tour explores a time when the area served as London’s notorious red-light district, focusing on the lives of those forced into illicit trades or marginalized by the stringent moral laws of the day. The walk will share the stories of those who lived, worked and played in the area in days gone by.
address: Opposite Covent Garden Underground Station, WC2E 9JT

name: Shaftesbury Hall
description:
Shaftesbury Hall is a Tin Tabernacle  rebuilt by North London Samaritans in 2018 to replicate the original Hall built in the 1890s.
It has been owned by North London Samaritans for 50 years and since the rebuild is used as a Community Hub, with our branch of Samaritans at the rear.

name: Silvertown: A sailor's story
description: Silvertown is a newly regenerated area in the borough of Newham, being re-equipped to provide infrastructure for its burgeoning community. Nevertheless, we will be walking through an unconventional urban landscape to identify the daring narratives of mercantile activity, workers protests, and industrial innovations along the way. This tour ends with a tour of Tipping Point East - a new circular economy hub.
address: London City Hall, Kamal Chunchie Way, E16 1ZE

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Bartholomew's Hospital
description: The Grade I listed North Wing at St Bartholomew’s Hospital in the City of London houses two of England’s most important interiors, the Great Hall, and the Hogarth Stair with its large paintings by William Hogarth. The hospital was designed by architect James Gibbs and construction of the North Wing was completed in 1732.
address: St Bartholomew's Hospital, West Smithfield, EC1A 7BE

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St Ethelburga's Centre for Reconciliation and Peace
description: Small late 14C church largely destroyed by a bomb in 1993. Restored as a centre for reconciliation and peace using Medieval building techniques and original materials. Unique Bedouin tent in peace garden.

name: St George in the East
description: Splendid Baroque exterior. Interior destroyed in the Blitz and rebuilt to new design by Martin Bailey in 1963.
address: Cannon Street Road The Highway  E1, E1 0BH

name: St George's Bloomsbury
description: St George's Bloomsbury is one of the twelve new churches designed and paid for under the 1711 Act of Parliament for building fifty new Churches, and the sixth and final London Church designed by Hawksmoor.

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary the Virgin Primrose Hill
description: St Mary's is a Victorian church famous for its second vicar Percy Dearmer who together with Ralph Vaughn Williams produced the English Hymnal in 1906.  We have a rich history of Church Music, beautiful worship and  vestments.  We also have a passion for  social justice within our community.  We were the first parish in Edmonton Diocese to have a woman vicar.
address: St Mary's Primrose Hill, Elsworthy Road, NW3 3DJ

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Pancras Church & Crypt
description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
address: Euston Road/Upper Woburn Place NW1, NW1 2BA

name: St Thomas with St Matthew, Clapton Common
description: Originally, built in 1773 as the Stamford Hill Chapel, St Thomas' are "Citizens with the Saints". The Heritage Lottery Fund, local artists, and academics are working with the church to engage and preserve how we work together as 'commoners' and 'caretakers for the 'common good'. Explore this in the Exhibition - On Common Ground - and become part of St Thomas' Future for the Common Good.
address: 1 Clapton Terrace, Clapton Common, Hackney, E5 9BW

name: Stratford Waterfront at East Bank
description: The Stratford Waterfront masterplan unites V&A East Museum, UAL: London College of Fashion, the BBC Music Studios, and Sadler’s Wells East into London’s most significant cultural district for 150 years. This walking tour will share the story behind the masterplan and the 1.5ha of new landscape delivered, which has created a welcoming public space and broadened access to culture for all.

name: Streatham Hill Theatre
description: As part of the Open House Festival, Streatham Hill Theatre stands out as a significant example of London’s theatrical heritage. Built in 1928–29, it was the final theatre designed by renowned architect W. G. R. Sprague. Opening in 1929, the venue hosted theatre, opera, ballet and variety performances until 1962, with a temporary closure between 1944 and 1950 due to wartime bomb damage.

name: The Building Centre
description: Explore the Building Centre, a landmark home for architecture and the built environment in the heart of London. Discover its distinctive modernist spaces, public galleries and exhibitions, and learn how the building has brought together architects, designers, makers and city-shapers for more than 90 years.

name: The Cartoon Museum
description: Underground museum. Interior design by Sam Jacobs Studio. Design concept influenced by cartoon and comic narrative techniques.
address: The Cartoon Museum, 63 Wells St, W1A 3AE

name: The City Churches: St Stephen Walbrook
description: Wren's own and 'finest City Church'.  Fantastic architecture with different shapes,  twelve Corinthian columns and covered by huge dome - first of its type. Central stone altar by Henry Moore installed in 1987. Birthplace of the Samaritans.

name: The City at night
description: Working, sleeping, playing – the City of London is home to all sorts of activities after dark. This walking tour will explore buildings and spaces, well known and lesser-known, in darkness, and will tell the history of night-time in London. We will visit places where London works, sleeps and plays at night, and over the course of two hours will even see how night time activity shifts.

name: The Purpose of Light: Exhibition by Misan Harriman
description: The Purpose of Light, Misan Harriman’s landmark photographic exhibition, bears witness to significant  moments, not with judgment or ideology, but with a deep and unflinching empathy for the human condition. Featuring 110 unique photographs, this exhibition is a call not for division, but for togetherness.

name: The West End At War
description: A special exhibition exploring the people and places that shaped the area during the Second World War. Tracing famous figures who made Soho their home, and the ordinary everyday heroes who kept the area functioning and our spirits up!

name: Tipping Point East site tour
description: Tour of Newham's first circular economy construction hub and home of our founding partners Yes Make, Material Cultures and RESOLVE Collective's Material Store. Learn about bio-circular practices and material reuse processes on site.

name: Tooting: Places, people and planning – a brief walk through time
description: Discover Tooting’s transformation from rural village to vibrant town. Starting at Tooting Bec and following the ancient Roman Stane Street, this one-mile tour contrasts historic views with today's high street. Explore iconic building facades, changing shops, and post-war migration. See how planning has shaped the area and what the future holds for this evolving neighborhood.

name: Traditional Roofing in Hampstead Garden Suburb
description: This guided tour will examine the traditional roofs of Hampstead Garden Suburb. These roofs were designed by early twentieth century architects, seeking to revitalise the centuries-old tradition of English roofing crafts largely lost during the process of industrialisation. By looking up, we will discover the quirky nature of heritage roofs and the conservation challenges they pose today.

name: Walking Tour:  Charles I - Monster or Martyr ?
description: Walking tour of the sites of the last days of King Charles I and the legacy of the upheavals which cost him his life and still echo to this day.

name: Westminster Abbey – East End
description: UNESCO World Heritage site dating from 11th century including stunning examples of Gothic and Medieval architecture and many hidden treasures.

name: Wiener Holocaust Library
description:
The Wiener Holocaust Library is one of the world’s leading and most extensive archives on the Holocaust. 
From 1939 to 1945, 20 million individuals were exploited as slave and forced labourers by the Nazi regime. Our latest exhibition 'Nazi Slave Labour: Perpetrators and Victims' explores how perpetrators profited off and exploited slave labourers, alongside the first-hand stories of the victims.

name: Worlds End Studios
description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.
